question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,2,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(2,-1,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-3)\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12-6-4|}{\sqrt{16+4+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-22|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{11}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
